rachel: saw unusual spike in resume-replay cases after we flipped new routing TTL. console shows same resume token attached twice within seconds :confused:
vik: sample? logs?
rachel: snippet:
```
[proxy] 2026-04-02T09:02:47Z conn=0xdead idle_close=25s FIN_SENT route=sticky-7
[runtime] 2026-04-02T09:02:47Z session=safe resume=tok-900 kv=hit
[client] 2026-04-02T09:02:48Z reconnect resume=tok-900 fingerprint=client-fp=none -> new session created
```
omar: note the client from older SDKs sends no fingerprint header, we relied on x-client-id but some clients send x-client-fingerprintv2. mismatch causes runtime to treat as different client and bill
sonya: ops: short-term add console dedupe window and annotate alert to reduce noise. long-term either normalize fingerprint header at proxy or accept resume when token matches and heuristics show same IP/UA
vik: quick runtime patch: if resume token exists and incoming has no fingerprint but IP+UA match last_seen, allow non-billable attach and emit audit. pseudo:
```
if token_exists(tok) and (fingerprint_match or heuristic_ipua_match):
  attach_nonbillable()
else:
  create_billable()
```
rachel: need to be careful with IP spoofing; limit heuristic to same /24 and same UA + short last_seen window (<=3s)
omar: also add metric resume.heuristic_attach and a flag runtime.ff.heuristic_reattach
sonya: will gate proxy header normalization behind FF and roll to 5% first. console: add banner "resume heuristic in flight" and dedupe alerts for 30s
deploy-bot: deploy requested: canary/runtime/heuristic-reattach -> queued on eng-runtime-canary
vik: I'll open PR with tests for missing-fingerprint case and add e2e that simulates older SDKs
rachel: I'll notify CS and include which tenants were affected
sonya: agree. postmortem item: consider standardizing x-resume-fingerprint header in client SDKs and server-side proxy enforcement
rachel: thanks team. monitoring: watch resume.heuristic_attach, billing.delta, active_sockets_per_token. update when canary finishes :eyes:
